title: KV: Granular Reuse Map and Spill Signal Dampener
author: Sophia Martinez
description:
Motivation: Production traffic has visible oscillation between aggressive spill cycles and immediate refill for small-object-heavy tenants. This causes repeated paging, short-lived memory pressure spikes, and tail-latency regressions during bursty workloads. Existing eviction policies favor simple LRU or slab-based heuristics which do not encode per-tenant reuse locality nor dampen rapid pressure signals from the IO/spill subsystem.

Summary: Introduces two complementary mechanisms to reduce fragmentation-driven spill churn and improve steady-state token-serving latency: 1) a Granular Reuse Map (GRM) — a compact, per-tenant map that tracks slot-level reuse heat and preferred free-slot candidates for fast allocation without triggering global compaction; 2) a Spill Signal Dampener — a small, configurable controller in the KV pressure path that accumulates and smooths spill demand signals (with hysteresis and rate limits) so that spill/compaction work is scheduled less reactively and with fewer oscillations. The change includes metrics, a limited-capacity background compact worker, a scheduler tweak to prefer local slot reclamation tasks, and an opt-in config flag for gradual rollout.

Implementation details: - GRM is implemented as a bounded, lock-sharded structure attached to tenant descriptors (src/serving/kv/grm_allocator.go). It maintains a lightweight bloom-like recency fingerprint plus a free-slot candidate ring; allocations consult GRM first to find reuse-friendly slots. - The Spill Signal Dampener (src/serving/kv/spill_dampener.go) converts instantaneous pressure events into an exponentially-weighted accumulator with a cooldown window; only when accumulated pressure crosses a tenant-specific threshold does it schedule a bounded compact job. Dampener parameters are tunable via tenant config and default to conservative values. - compact_worker.go implements a rate-limited background compactor that performs local slot coalescing (scoped to tenant and slab class) and returns reclaimed slots to the GRM. Compaction uses short windows to avoid CPU spikes. - Scheduler integration (pkg/scheduler/compact_policy.go) prioritizes compact jobs that are likely to reduce fragmentation without triggering remote spill. - Metrics added under internal/metrics/kv_frag_metrics.go: grm_hit_ratio, dampener_pressure, scheduled_compactions, compaction_duration_ms, and spill_cycles_prevented. - Tests: microbenchmarks and e2e scenarios added in tests/kv/grm_bench_test.go that simulate small-object churn and bursty writes.

Rollout plan: Feature is gated behind kv.grm_enabled and kv.spill_dampener_enabled tenant flags. Default rollout: enable in canary region for 24 hours, monitor grm_hit_ratio and spill_cycles_prevented, then expand to 20% of tenants, then to all. There is an emergency opt-out via tenant-scoped toggle and an operator-level override to disable background compactor immediately.

Benchmarks & results: On our synthetic small-object churn suite (10k tenants, median object size 176B, burst windows 200ms), observed results after enabling GRM + Dampener: - median P95 token latency improved by ~6.8% under burst (service layer); - number of spill cycles reduced by 71% in steady state; - cumulative CPU used by background compaction stayed under configured budget (default 4 cores across nodes) and did not materially affect serving throughput; - memory residency improved (fewer transient allocations) leading to 12% lower peak host memory usage during bursts. Full benchmark logs attached in PR artifacts.

Testing: Unit tests for GRM invariants and dampener behavior added. Integration tests simulate Tenants A/B under mixed read/write and confirm no regression in eviction correctness. CI runs include new microbench harness; added automated smoke test that toggles tenant flags to validate safe opt-out.

Compatibility & safety: Changes are backward-compatible: when flags are off, behaviour is unchanged. Parameters are conservative by default. Compaction is rate-limited and scoped to avoid cross-tenant interference. There are additional telemetry alerts (alert rule names included in docs) to surface unexpected compaction or spill patterns.

Docs/RFC: New design doc and rollout instructions at docs/rfc/2025-07-grm-spill-dampener.md. The PR includes guidance for SRE on dashboards to watch and suggested thresholds for the dampener.

Why this is different from past approaches: Prior PRs focused on monolithic slab compaction or eviction heuristics that react immediately to pressure. GRM changes allocation-time locality behavior to reduce fragmentation at the source, while the Dampener avoids oscillatory compaction/ spill scheduling — together they yield lower spill churn without centralizing compaction or increasing worst-case CPU.

Requested action: review for algorithmic edge cases around concurrent slot reclamation and correctness of the dampener thresholds; suggestions on metric naming and alert thresholds welcome.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Can we bound the worst-case CPU the compactor will consume per node? Please add an abort condition when host CPU > 70%.
Author (Sophia Martinez): Added a soft budget and an immediate abort hook when host-level CPU exceeds configured threshold; documented in the compactor code and RFC.
Ravi Singh: The dampener threshold feels tenant-sensitive. Can we make it proportional to tenant steady-state allocation rather than absolute bytes?
Author: Dampener now uses tenant-resident-window-normalized pressure (configured by tenant_weight). Added tests to validate behavior across small and large tenants.
Mei Chen: Unit test failure on race in GRM with concurrent frees + scans; please ensure proper sharding/locks.
Author: Fixed by converting the candidate ring to lock-sharded segments with compare-and-swap updates; re-ran tests and added deterministic concurrency test.
Liam O'Connor: Approving after minor nits on metric names; leaving final approval for Ravi.
Ravi Singh: Approving. Observability looks good; recommend enabling for canary immediately.
release_notes: Introduce opt-in GRM (Granular Reuse Map) and Spill Signal Dampener to reduce fragmentation-driven spill churn and improve latency under small-object churn; gated by tenant flags kv.grm_enabled and kv.spill_dampener_enabled. Includes metrics and a controlled background compactor. Non-breaking; disabled by default.
